To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the continuous time distributed convex optimization dynamics for undirected graphs cannot be directly applied to the directed setting; and (ii) a novel continuous time distributed convex minimization dynamics can be designed for directed graphs, and is guaranteed to converge to the set of global minima of the sum of the convex functions, on any strongly-connected weight-balanced digraph.

(i) a consensus based distributed optimization dynamics fails to converge on directed graphs, (ii) an alternative distributed optimization dynamics converges to the set of minima on any strongly connected directed graph.

(i) consensus based dynamics fails to solve the distributed optimization problem on directed graphs, and (ii) we design a novel distributed dynamics that solves the optimization problem on any strongly connected and weight balanced digraph.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a distributed optimization problem in continuous time on directed graphs and we provide a solution that works for any strongly connected weight-balanced digraph.
the design of distributed algorithms for the solution of convex optimization problems on networks of agents, and with the study of the properties of such algorithms.
the following questions: What are the necessary conditions on the underlying graph topology to ensure convergence of the distributed optimization problem?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the consensus dynamics that solves the distributed optimization problem in the undirected scenario, fails in the directed setting, but the proposed dynamics is guaranteed to converge on any strongly connected weighted digraph.

, the consensus based dynamics is guaranteed to converge for any strongly connected undirected graph and for any strongly connected weight-balanced digraph; and the gradient based dynamics is guaranteed for any strongly connected digraph.
, the continuous time dynamics for distributed convex optimization on directed graphs is guaranteed to converge if the underlying graph is weight balanced and strongly connected.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a new dynamics for the distributed optimization problem over directed graphs.
we provide a necessary and sufficient condition on the digraph to guarantee the convergence of a distributed optimization problem, and design an algorithm that satisfies this condition.

we show that a continuous time distributed algorithm for the optimization of convex functions over undirected graphs can be transcribed to the digraph setting, provided that the digraph satisfies some simple conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a consensus based dynamics, when transcribed to a directed scenario, may not converge, but a simple modification of this dynamics, which is inspired by the notion of weight balancing, is guaranteed to converge to the optimal set.
the dynamics that solves the distributed convex optimization problem in the undirected case is not guaranteed to solve the problem in the directed case.
a simple modification of the dynamics can be made so as to solve the optimization problem on a weight balanced digraph instead of an undirected graph.
